title: The Pipe and the Canal
subtitle: 气候变化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）
meta: 主题语境：气候变化（环境保护·气候变化）　|　核心词汇：means　|　正文 319 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 means 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Our village has no river, and for three summers the rain came late. In the old days water arrived in buckets. Today a plastic pipe brings it from a spring four kilometres away ① by means of gravity alone. The pipe was laid by eleven families, none of them rich, and it works precisely because nothing in it needs electricity.

My grandfather distrusts anything that needs electricity. 'A pump breaks in August,' he says, 'which is when you need it most.' He prefers the slower ② means — a canal, a jar, a tree planted twenty years ago for somebody else. The cheapest ③ means of carrying water, he will tell anybody who asks, is still a shoulder pole, because it cannot break.

Adaptation is a word officials like, and in practice it is much duller than that. When the district offered tanks to the eleven families, my uncle said: '④ By all means take the tank, but dig the channel first.' He meant that hardware fails and habits do not. The drought two years ago taught us the same lesson ⑤ by no means gently.

'Are we rich?' I once asked my grandmother. 'We have ⑥ means,' she answered carefully, 'but we live inside them.' I did not understand her then. Owning a pump ⑦ means nothing at all if nobody maintains it, and I think that is close to what she intended: even the poorest household in our street still possesses the means to plant one tree.

So the canal was dug, eleven spades wide, in the last week of March. It looks like nothing at all from the road. Yet a canal is not an end in itself; it is simply a ⑧ means to an end, and every habit we keep ⑨ means the difference between one bad summer and three. Slow means, I have learned, rarely fail. Choosing the right ⑩ means is a slower business than choosing quickly, and lasts considerably longer.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 方法；手段；途径
B. n. 财力；财富（常指维持生活的收入）
C. n. （交通、运输的）工具；方式
D. v. 意味着；说明……也很重要（第三人称单数）
E. 固定搭配：by means of 凭借；用……的办法
F. 固定搭配：by no means 决不；一点也不
G. 固定搭配：by all means 当然可以；务必
H. 固定搭配：a means to an end 达到目的的手段

items.q: The cheapest means of carrying water
By all means take the tank
Owning a pump means nothing at all
it is simply a means to an end
every habit we keep means the difference

answers.why: by means of＋手段，意为“凭借、用……的办法”，此处说只靠重力引水。
the slower means 意为“较慢的办法”，指祖父偏爱的一整套传统做法。
the cheapest means of carrying water 指运水的工具／方式，后文的扁担正是一种运输方式。
by all means 意为“当然可以、尽管去做”，叔叔同意领水箱，但提出前置条件。
by no means 意为“决不”，修饰 gently，说明那场干旱给人的教训毫不温和。
have means 指“有一定财力”，祖母强调家境尚可但必须量入为出。
means＋宾语 nothing，是动词“意味着、说明……很有价值”，强调维护的重要性。
a means to an end 意为“达成目的的手段”，水渠本身不是目的，而是解决缺水的办法。
同样作动词，意为“意味着”，说明坚持的习惯决定能否度过干旱。
the right means 指正确的“方法、途径”，与第 2 题同义复现。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 那条管子只靠重力把水引过来。（by means of）
挑水最便宜的工具仍然是扁担。（means n.）
他说：“当然要领水箱，但先把渠挖好。”（by all means）
那场干旱毫不温和地教会了我们这个道理。（by no means）
如果没有人维护，拥有一台水泵毫无意义。（mean v.）
挖渠本身不是目的，而是达成目的的手段。（a means to an end）
answers: The pipe brings the water here by means of gravity alone.
The cheapest means of carrying water is still a shoulder pole.
'By all means take the tank,' he said, 'but dig the channel first'.
That drought taught us the lesson by no means gently.
Owning a pump means nothing at all if nobody maintains it.
Digging the canal is not the end in itself but a means to an end.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 means 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Our village has no river, so a plastic pipe brings water by means of gravity alone.
My grandfather prefers slower means, because the cheapest means of carrying water is a shoulder pole, which cannot break.
When the district offered tanks, my uncle said: 'By all means take the tank, but dig the channel first.'
The drought taught us the same lesson by no means gently, and owning a pump means nothing without somebody to maintain it.
'Are we rich?' I asked; 'We have means,' my grandmother said, 'but we live inside them.'
A canal is only a means to an end, yet choosing the right means decides whether a village survives one bad summer or three.
